intro: You're looking for an HR consultant near you, likely because something has come up at work that needs an experienced outside view. Perhaps you're dealing with a tricky employee issue, updating your policies, or planning a restructure, and you want someone local who can advise you directly. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK HR consultant, who will quote you directly for the work.
need_heading: What people searching for an HR consultant near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching for an HR consultant near me need practical, confidential help with a people problem that can't wait.
needs: You need to handle a disciplinary or grievance procedure correctly and want advice on the process before you take the next step.
You're updating your staff handbook or contracts and want them checked so they match what actually happens in your workplace.
You're planning to recruit new staff and need help with job descriptions, interview questions and offer letters.
You're considering a restructure or redundancy situation and want guidance on how to do it fairly and lawfully.
You're a small business owner with no HR team and need someone nearby who can answer questions as they arise.
context_heading: What to understand about HR consultancy and regulation
context: HR consultancy work is not regulated by a single body, so it pays to check credentials yourself. Many HR professionals are members of the CIPD, which shows a commitment to professional standards and training. Ask about their experience with situations like yours and request references from similar clients.

Where your issue touches on employment law, a consultant should be clear about the limits of their role and when you need a solicitor. For high-risk matters such as tribunals or complex dismissals, getting legal advice alongside HR support is sensible.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the situation you need help with, such as a disciplinary, a restructure or a policy update.
Say how many employees your organisation has, so the consultant understands the scale of your operation.
Mention your location and how far you're willing to travel, since you're looking for someone near you.
Explain whether you need a one-off piece of work or ongoing support.
Include any deadlines you're working towards, such as a hearing date or a planned announcement.
Note if you already have legal advisers involved, so the consultant knows who else is in the picture.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the HR consultant
questions: What experience do you have with situations like mine?
Are you a member of the CIPD or another relevant professional body?
How do you charge for your work, and what will that include?
Will you be handling my case personally, or will someone else in your team do the work?
How will you keep my information confidential?
When would you recommend I also speak to a solicitor?

faqs.q: Do I need an HR consultant or a solicitor?
faqs.a: An HR consultant can advise on policies, procedures and employee relations, while a solicitor provides legal advice. For high-risk issues like tribunal claims or complex dismissals, you may need both. A consultant should tell you when legal advice is appropriate.

faqs.q: How do I check an HR consultant's credentials?
faqs.a: Ask about their professional memberships, such as the CIPD, and their experience with similar situations. Request references from comparable clients and ask about their approach to confidentiality. Since HR consultancy is not regulated by a single body, these checks are important.

faqs.q: Can an HR consultant help with staff handbooks?
faqs.a: Yes, HR consultants often update staff handbooks to make sure they reflect current practice and are legally compliant. They can also advise on contracts, policies and procedures.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to a consultant?
faqs.a: Gather any relevant documents, such as contracts, policies, correspondence and notes of meetings. Think about what outcome you want and any deadlines you're working towards. This will help the consultant understand your situation quickly.

extra_heading: What a first meeting with a local HR consultant involves
extra: When you first speak to an HR consultant near you, they will usually start by asking you to describe the situation in your own words and will want to see any relevant documents, such as contracts, policies or correspondence. This helps them understand the facts and the context before offering any views. They may also ask about your organisation's size, structure and any deadlines you are working towards.

The consultant will then explain how they might help, what the process could involve and how they charge for their work. They should be clear about what they can and cannot do, and will tell you if the matter needs a solicitor or another specialist. You should feel able to ask questions about their experience and approach.

After the meeting, you should have a clearer idea of your options and the next steps. The consultant may provide a written summary or a proposal for work, which you can consider before deciding whether to proceed. Remember that iComply does not provide the advice itself; we simply introduce you to a consultant who quotes you directly.

extra_faqs.q: Will the consultant come to my workplace?
extra_faqs.a: Many HR consultants offer both remote and in-person meetings. Since you are looking for someone near you, you can ask whether they are willing to visit your premises. This can be helpful for matters that require a physical presence, such as employee meetings or document reviews.

extra_faqs.q: How quickly can I see an HR consultant near me?
extra_faqs.a: Availability varies, so it is best to ask the consultant directly when you speak to them. Some may be able to offer an initial conversation quickly, while others may have a waiting list. iComply does not set timeframes, but we can introduce you to a consultant who can discuss their availability.
